name: The Takeshi Kaneshiro Tree

location.address: Mr. Brown Avenue (Bolang Dadao), Chishang Township, Taitung County, Taiwan

story:
A farmer planted this tree so he had somewhere to tie his cattle. Wu A-mu put it in around the 1970s, a single bishop wood in the middle of his rice paddy, good for shade and a tether and nothing else. In June 2013 EVA Air filmed a television commercial under it with the actor Takeshi Kaneshiro, and within a year the tree had a nickname, a fence around its roots, and an estimated NT$500 million a year in visitor spending attached to it. It also had photographers walking into the crop to get the shot.

Then on 23 July 2014 Typhoon Matmo pushed it over. Japanese arborists Yamashita Tokuo and Kawaguchi Yoshihisa came out with Taiwanese colleagues, righted it within days and treated it where it stood, and it was replanted on the same spot. It has grown steadily since and came through Typhoon Haikui in September 2023 with a few broken branches.

The sponsorship contract expired in 2023 and the official name reverted to the Fengcha Tree, the tea-offering tree. Nobody calls it that. It is about ten metres tall, barely a metre around the trunk, still alone in the paddy, and Mr. Brown Avenue past it is a farm road closed to cars. The usual approach is a rented bicycle from Chishang station and five kilometres of rice with no traffic on it.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by being the only tree out there: one broad crown about ten metres high standing alone in the rice, with a low fence around its roots. It stands beside Mr. Brown Avenue, the farm road out of Chishang.
access: Free. Stands in a working rice paddy beside Mr. Brown Avenue (Bolang Dadao), a farm road closed to cars but open to bikes and pedestrians; the tree is fenced to protect its roots but fully visible and photographable from the path.
transport: Chishang Railway Station, then about 5 km (roughly 30 minutes) by rented bicycle along Mr. Brown Avenue; bike rental stalls sit right outside the station.

name: The Sianglin Sacred Tree
age_estimate: disputed: about 626 years by the newest study, versus a long-quoted 2,300 years

location.address: Trail 1 (the giant-tree boardwalk), beside Ciyun Temple and Xianglin Elementary School, Alishan National Forest Recreation Area, Alishan Township, Chiayi County, Taiwan

story:
This tree was elected. Alishan's original Sacred Tree, a red cypress of around 3,000 years, was wrecked by storm damage and taken down in the late 1990s, and the Forestry Bureau put the succession to a public online vote. About 25,000 people took part, this cypress won, and on 1 January 2007 the county magistrate crowned it Alishan's second-generation Sacred Tree. Before that it went by Guangwu Cypress, after a provincial governor's conviction that it had germinated during the reign of the Han emperor Guangwu.

Its age is genuinely in dispute, and both numbers are worth carrying. Tourism material has said roughly 2,300 years for decades, some of it stretching to 3,000. Then a 2022 tree-ring study by National Chiayi University, commissioned by the Forestry Bureau, dated the main trunk at about 626 years and explained the gap: what looks like one enormous stem is a merged tree, several red cypresses that grew into each other over centuries. The bulk is real. The single great age is not established, and the older figure is still the one most of the tourism material carries.

The park's own record gives it 45 metres of height and 12.3 metres of girth; an older account says 43.5 and 13.1. It stands on Trail 1, a 600 metre boardwalk near Ciyun Temple that passes the Thousand-Year Cypress and the Tree of Three Generations on the way, so it is a short walk in and not the only giant on it.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the trunk, 12.3 metres round and visibly several stems fused into one mass. It stands on Trail 1, the boardwalk running between Ciyun Temple and Xianglin Elementary School.
access: Paid entry to Alishan National Forest Recreation Area (around NT$300, less for Taiwan residents/students), open year round; from the park entrance it is a short, easy walk along the paved 600 m Trail 1 boardwalk past Ciyun Temple.
transport: Alishan Forest Railway or bus (Alishan Route B) from Chiayi Railway Station, roughly 2.5 to 3 hours; alight at Alishan Bus Station just outside the park's official entrance gate, then walk in.
